anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level SQL and transaction design forces the engine to touch far more data or hold locks far longer than the business requirement demands.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Metadata about data distribution is stale, missing, or misleading, causing systematic cardinality misestimates and sub-optimal plan choices.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Instance-level settings for memory, parallelism, checkpoints, logging, and background workers are mis-tuned for the actual hardware and workload.

When all three root causes appear together, symptoms compound: the same business operation may exhibit runaway latency, wildly fluctuating execution plans, and resource waits that do not match real hardware utilization. Statements already written with broad scans or chatty row-by-row access patterns are paired with estimates that radically under- or over-count rows, steering the optimizer toward plans that spill to disk, fan out nested-loop joins, or serialize otherwise parallelizable work. Mis-sized work memory and buffer pools then exaggerate I/O bursts, trigger checkpoint storms, and prolong lock holding, while disabled or throttled statistics maintenance hides the true row-count drift. The resulting picture in monitoring views is a confusing mix of slow queries, frequent plan recompiles, memory pressure, idle hardware, and application timeouts.

Causally, the inefficient SQL logic inflates the volume of data the optimizer must reason about, making it hypersensitive to statistics quality. Stale or coarse statistics mislead the cost model, often selecting plans whose fragility is exposed by the oversized SQL patterns. Meanwhile, mis-configured memory, parallelism, or checkpoint cadence both throttles automatic statistics refresh and limits the engine’s ability to amortize the extra work, feeding back into even staler statistics and longer execution times. Each layer therefore reinforces the next: poor SQL magnifies the impact of bad statistics; bad statistics force plan paths that are intolerant of resource mis-tuning; and mis-tuned parameters slow the corrective mechanisms that could otherwise mitigate SQL or statistics flaws, driving a self-sustaining performance spiral.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
